meta.how_to_read: entities are grouped by type; every relationship carries evidence (pep, section, rule, snippet) pointing at the raw text it was extracted from; rule names refer to src/extract.py and notes/design.md

PEP.doc: A Python Enhancement Proposal in or referenced by the slice (number, title, status, type, python_version, in_slice).

Construct.doc: A named typing feature you import or use: a class, special form, qualifier, decorator or function (e.g. TypedDict, ParamSpec).

Syntax.doc: A piece of language notation rather than an importable name (e.g. `X | Y`, `list[int]`, `class C[T]`, `(int) -> str`).

Problem.doc: A recurring motivation: something users or tools struggled with that one or more PEPs set out to fix.

RejectedIdea.doc: An alternative that a PEP considered and rejected, postponed or answered an objection to; carries the reason given.

PythonVersion.doc: A CPython feature release (from the Python-Version header).

TypeChecker.doc: A static type checker or IDE named as implementing a PEP (mypy, pyright, Pyre, pytype, PyCharm).

SUPERSEDES.doc: The source PEP replaced the target PEP (from the Replaces / Superseded-By header fields).

BUILDS_ON.doc: The source PEP relies on or extends the target PEP: a reference outside rejected-ideas sections, weighted by the section it sits in.

INTRODUCES.doc: The source PEP defined the construct or syntax (or proposed it, if the PEP was rejected or withdrawn; the reasoner checks the status).

EXTENDS.doc: The source PEP changes or adds to a construct or syntax that a different PEP introduced (title or abstract mentions it as code).

ADDRESSES_PROBLEM.doc: The source PEP was written to fix the problem (cue phrases in its Abstract, Motivation or Rationale).

REJECTED_ALTERNATIVE.doc: The source PEP considered this alternative and rejected, postponed or objected to it (one idea per subsection or bullet of a rejected-ideas section).

CONCERNS.doc: What a rejected idea was about: constructs, syntax, problems or PEPs mentioned in the idea's heading or text.

AVAILABLE_IN.doc: The PEP shipped in (or, if rejected/withdrawn, targeted) this Python version, from the Python-Version header.

IMPLEMENTED_BY.doc: A type checker is named in the PEP's implementation sections as implementing or prototyping it.

evidence_fields.snippet: the text (<= ~200 chars) that triggered the rule
